scenes.title: OUTRO: WHAT IT MEANS FOR YOU

chunks.text: October 29th, 2026.
chunks.tts: October twenty-ninth, twenty twenty-six.

chunks.text: 8:05 PM, UTC.
chunks.tts: eight oh five P M, U T C.

chunks.text: On ten blockchains, within minutes, money starts leaving Binance — the biggest crypto exchange on Earth.
chunks.tts: On ten blockchains, within minutes, money starts leaving Binance — the biggest crypto exchange on Earth.

chunks.text: Not thousands.
chunks.tts: Not thousands.

chunks.text: Not millions.
chunks.tts: Not millions.

chunks.text: Billions.
chunks.tts: Billions.

chunks.text: Within about twenty minutes, most of an estimated six point three billion dollars is gone.
chunks.tts: Within about twenty minutes, most of an estimated six point three billion dollars is gone.

chunks.text: Nobody cracked a safe.
chunks.tts: Nobody cracked a safe.

chunks.text: Binance says it has found no evidence that a single private key was leaked.
chunks.tts: Binance says it has found no evidence that a single private key was leaked.

chunks.text: Instead, its first investigation pointed somewhere far more ordinary…
chunks.tts: Instead, its first investigation pointed somewhere far more ordinary…

chunks.text: an engineer's laptop.
chunks.tts: an engineer's laptop.

chunks.text: This is the story of the biggest crypto heist ever recorded — how the attackers got in, how they emptied the wallets, the race to freeze the money…
chunks.tts: This is the story of the biggest crypto heist ever recorded — how the attackers got in, how they emptied the wallets, the race to freeze the money…

chunks.text: and the one question nobody can answer yet.
chunks.tts: and the one question nobody can answer yet.

chunks.text: To understand the size of this, you need to understand Binance.
chunks.tts: To understand the size of this, you need to understand Binance.

chunks.text: It's the world's largest crypto exchange, with around 335 million registered users.
chunks.tts: It's the world's largest crypto exchange, with around three hundred thirty-five million registered users.

chunks.text: In its 2025 annual report, it said it held about 162.8 billion dollars in assets under custody.
chunks.tts: In its twenty twenty-five annual report, it said it held about one hundred sixty-two point eight billion dollars in assets under custody.

chunks.text: An exchange doesn't keep all of that in one place.
chunks.tts: An exchange doesn't keep all of that in one place.

chunks.text: Think of a store.
chunks.tts: Think of a store.

chunks.text: Most of the money sits in the vault — cold wallets, kept offline, slow and hard to reach.
chunks.tts: Most of the money sits in the vault — cold wallets, kept offline, slow and hard to reach.

chunks.text: The rest stays in the cash register — hot wallets — online, so people can withdraw at any second.
chunks.tts: The rest stays in the cash register — hot wallets — online, so people can withdraw at any second.

chunks.text: The cash register is convenient.
chunks.tts: The cash register is convenient.

chunks.text: It's also the part of the building that faces the street.
chunks.tts: It's also the part of the building that faces the street.

chunks.text: And Binance already knew what happens when someone reaches into it.
chunks.tts: And Binance already knew what happens when someone reaches into it.

chunks.text: Because it had happened before.
chunks.tts: Because it had happened before.

chunks.text: May 7th, 2019.
chunks.tts: May seventh, twenty nineteen.
seventeen fifteen U T C.

chunks.text: One transaction pulls seven thousand Bitcoin out of Binance's hot wallet — about forty million dollars at the time.
chunks.tts: One transaction pulls seven thousand Bitcoin out of Binance's hot wallet — about forty million dollars at the time.

chunks.text: Binance later explained: hackers had collected user API keys, two-factor codes and other information — through phishing, viruses and other attacks.
chunks.tts: Binance later explained: hackers had collected user A P I keys, two-factor codes and other information — through phishing, viruses and other attacks.

chunks.text: Then they waited.
chunks.tts: Then they waited.

chunks.text: Binance said the hackers "had the patience to wait" — striking through seemingly unrelated accounts, with a withdrawal built to pass every security check.
chunks.tts: Binance said the hackers "had the patience to wait" — striking through seemingly unrelated accounts, with a withdrawal built to pass every security check.

chunks.text: The alarms fired only after the money was gone.
chunks.tts: The alarms fired only after the money was gone.

chunks.text: In a livestream, CEO Changpeng Zhao — CZ — said Binance was considering an idea first raised by a Bitcoin developer: paying miners to rewrite the blockchain and undo the theft.
chunks.tts: In a livestream, C E O Chang Peng Jao — C Z — said Binance was considering an idea first raised by a Bitcoin developer: paying miners to rewrite the blockchain and undo the theft.

chunks.text: The backlash was immediate.
chunks.tts: The backlash was immediate.

chunks.text: Within a day, CZ dropped it, saying the Bitcoin ledger is "the most immutable ledger on the planet."
chunks.tts: Within a day, C Z dropped it, saying the Bitcoin ledger is "the most immutable ledger on the planet."

chunks.text: Binance covered the loss from SAFU — its Secure Asset Fund for Users, funded since 2018 with ten percent of trading fees.
chunks.tts: Binance covered the loss from Sayfoo — its Secure Asset Fund for Users, funded since twenty eighteen with ten percent of trading fees.

chunks.text: A week later, withdrawals were back.
chunks.tts: A week later, withdrawals were back.

chunks.text: In 2022, an attacker abused a bridge bug on Binance's own BNB Chain to create two million BNB out of thin air — and the chain was halted.
chunks.tts: In twenty twenty-two, an attacker abused a bridge bug on Binance's own B N B Chain to create two million B N B out of thin air — and the chain was halted.

chunks.text: Each time, the lesson was the same.
chunks.tts: Each time, the lesson was the same.

chunks.text: The weak point is never the math.
chunks.tts: The weak point is never the math.

chunks.text: It's everything around it.
chunks.tts: It's everything around it.

chunks.text: Now — back to October 2026.
chunks.tts: Now — back to October twenty twenty-six.

chunks.text: Binance's initial investigation suggested the incident may have started with a compromised laptop belonging to a DevOps engineer — one of the people who build and run the machinery behind the exchange.
chunks.tts: Binance's initial investigation suggested the incident may have started with a compromised laptop belonging to a dev ops engineer — one of the people who build and run the machinery behind the exchange.

chunks.text: From that laptop, an attacker reached what Binance calls a "service container" — part of its internal infrastructure — and from there, submitted unauthorized withdrawal transactions.
chunks.tts: From that laptop, an attacker reached what Binance calls a "service container" — part of its internal infrastructure — and from there, submitted unauthorized withdrawal transactions.

chunks.text: Hours later, Binance said it had found additional points of breach.
chunks.tts: Hours later, Binance said it had found additional points of breach.

chunks.text: Co-CEO Richard Teng put it bluntly: this was not a single "one-click" action.
chunks.tts: co-C E O Richard Teng put it bluntly: this was not a single "one-click" action.

chunks.text: The attacker did not simply use one engineer's permissions.
chunks.tts: The attacker did not simply use one engineer's permissions.

chunks.text: And it was planned.
chunks.tts: And it was planned.

chunks.text: According to blockchain analysts at TRM Labs, staging began at least thirty-six hours earlier, with small withdrawals from the crypto mixer Tornado Cash funding the attacker's operating wallet.
chunks.tts: According to blockchain analysts at T R M Labs, staging began at least thirty-six hours earlier, with small withdrawals from the crypto mixer Tornado Cash funding the attacker's operating wallet.

chunks.text: Investigators believe the attackers didn't need to steal the keys.
chunks.tts: Investigators believe the attackers didn't need to steal the keys.

chunks.text: They got Binance's own systems to sign for them.
chunks.tts: They got Binance's own systems to sign for them.

chunks.text: So how do you turn a laptop into six billion dollars?
chunks.tts: So how do you turn a laptop into six billion dollars?

chunks.text: You give yourself twenty minutes.
chunks.tts: You give yourself twenty minutes.
eight oh five P M.

chunks.text: The first funds start moving — on the XRP Ledger, where analysts count about 296 million dollars drained in the first four minutes.
chunks.tts: The first funds start moving — on the X R P Ledger, where analysts count about two hundred ninety-six million dollars drained in the first four minutes.

chunks.text: Ten networks follow — Bitcoin, Ethereum, Tron, Solana, and more.
chunks.tts: Ten networks follow — Bitcoin, Ethereum, Tron, Solana, and more.

chunks.text: On nine of them, it looks almost normal: ordinary transfers, signed by Binance's own wallets.
chunks.tts: On nine of them, it looks almost normal: ordinary transfers, signed by Binance's own wallets.

chunks.text: Ethereum is different.
chunks.tts: Ethereum is different.

chunks.text: At 8:20, one transaction targets a Binance hot wallet labeled "Binance 14."
chunks.tts: At eight twenty, one transaction targets a Binance hot wallet labeled "Binance fourteen."

chunks.text: Inside it: fifty authorizations — all signed with Binance 14's own key — using an Ethereum feature called EIP-7702, which lets a wallet hand its powers to a piece of code.
chunks.tts: Inside it: fifty authorizations — all signed with Binance 14's own key — using an Ethereum feature called E I P seventy-seven oh two, which lets a wallet hand its powers to a piece of code.

chunks.text: Why fifty?
chunks.tts: Why fifty?

chunks.text: Every wallet keeps a running count of its transactions.
chunks.tts: Every wallet keeps a running count of its transactions.

chunks.text: An authorization only works if it matches the right number — and the attacker didn't know which number Binance 14 was on.
chunks.tts: An authorization only works if it matches the right number — and the attacker didn't know which number Binance fourteen was on.

chunks.text: So they brought fifty signed permission slips, one for every possible number.
chunks.tts: So they brought fifty signed permission slips, one for every possible number.

chunks.text: Exactly one matched.
chunks.tts: Exactly one matched.

chunks.text: In that moment, Binance 14 stopped being Binance's wallet.
chunks.tts: In that moment, Binance fourteen stopped being Binance's wallet.

chunks.text: It was running the attacker's sweeper code.
chunks.tts: It was running the attacker's sweeper code.

chunks.text: In under four minutes, it emptied — about 167,000 ETH, roughly 1.6 billion USDT, and dozens of other tokens.
chunks.tts: In under four minutes, it emptied — about one hundred sixty-seven thousand E T H, roughly one point six billion U S D T, and dozens of other tokens.

chunks.text: By TRM's count, Ethereum alone accounted for about 3.8 billion dollars.
chunks.tts: By T R M's count, Ethereum alone accounted for about three point eight billion dollars.

chunks.text: On Bitcoin: 18,270 BTC — around 1.47 billion more.
chunks.tts: On Bitcoin: eighteen thousand two hundred seventy B T C — around one point four seven billion more.

chunks.text: Most of it was gone in about twenty minutes.
chunks.tts: Most of it was gone in about twenty minutes.

chunks.text: And then, around 11 PM, a second wave hit — on Avalanche and Polygon.
chunks.tts: And then, around eleven P M, a second wave hit — on Avalanche and Polygon.

chunks.text: While the money moved, a race began.
chunks.tts: While the money moved, a race began.

chunks.text: Some crypto can be frozen.
chunks.tts: Some crypto can be frozen.

chunks.text: Stablecoins like USDT and USDC are issued by companies that can lock tokens in a specific wallet.
chunks.tts: Stablecoins like U S D T and U S D C are issued by companies that can lock tokens in a specific wallet.

chunks.tts: At nine oh one P M, Tether froze about nine hundred seventy-one million U S D T in the attacker's main receiving wallet.

chunks.text: Three minutes later, Circle froze 823 million USDC.
chunks.tts: Three minutes later, Circle froze eight hundred twenty-three million U S D C.

chunks.text: Soon after, Binance posted for the first time: it was aware of "a potential security issue."
chunks.tts: Soon after, Binance posted for the first time: it was aware of "a potential security issue."

chunks.text: Ripple and World Liberty Financial froze their stablecoins too.
chunks.tts: Ripple and World Liberty Financial froze their stablecoins too.

chunks.tts: That night, Binance suspended withdrawals and promised to cover every loss.
